title: Unexpected Synthetic Routes to Lanthanide Chalcogenido Clusters: Sm8Se6(SePh)12(THF)8 and [Sm7S7(SePh)6(DME)7]+

material_class.structural_family: cubic Sm8Se6 cubane-type chalcogenido cluster with edge-bridging SePh and terminal THF

synthesis.procedure: Initially prepared by reacting Sm with PhSeSePh in THF and then treating the mixture with elemental Se, affording deep orange air-sensitive crystals of 1. Subsequent work showed Sm(SePh)2 as the source of Se2−; preparing Sm(SePh)2 in THF and allowing the divalent compound to decompose thermally at room temperature (chalcogen-free route) gave the largest and cleanest yield of 1. Identified by low-temperature single-crystal X-ray diffraction.

reagents.name: samarium(II) benzeneselenolate
reagents.role: divalent precursor that thermally generates Se2−

synthesis.vessel_or_method: solution synthesis followed by thermal decomposition of Sm(SePh)2; crystallization
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: deep orange air-sensitive crystals obtained and identified by low-temperature single-crystal X-ray diffraction
synthesis.yield: largest and cleanest yield obtained from the chalcogen-free thermal decomposition of Sm(SePh)2 (no numerical yield reported)

properties.summary: UV-vis absorption maximum at 341 nm attributed to ligand (SePh or Se2−) to Sm(III) charge transfer.

measurements.name: UV-vis absorption maximum
measurements.conditions: visible spectrum; assigned as ligand-to-Sm(III) charge transfer

material_class.structural_family: Sm7S7 cluster cation (two face-sharing square pyramids) with [Hg3(SePh)7]− counteranion

synthesis.procedure: Sm(SePh)3 was prepared by reducing Ph2Se2 with Sm/Hg amalgam. Slow addition of sulfur to Sm(SePh)3 in DME dissolved the precipitate; the orange solution turned light yellow before a yellow solid precipitated. When less than a full equivalent of S was added, light yellow air-sensitive crystals of [Sm7S7(SePh)6(DME)7][Hg3(SePh)7]·DME (2) were isolated and characterized by low-temperature single-crystal X-ray diffraction.

reagents.name: samarium/mercury amalgam
reagents.role: reductant generating Sm(SePh)3 and Hg-containing anion

reagents.name: elemental sulfur
reagents.role: sulfido source inserted into Ln–Se chemistry

synthesis.vessel_or_method: slow addition of sulfur to Sm(SePh)3 in DME
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: yellow solid precipitated; light yellow air-sensitive crystals of 2 isolated and characterized by low-temperature single-crystal X-ray diffraction

properties.summary: Unlike 1, the visible spectrum of 2 is featureless, suggesting that the visible absorption of 1 arises from Se2− to Sm(III) charge transfer rather than from SePh ligands.
